core.text: Observed: one 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and yielded final vial attenuations 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This bounded counterexample challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and stable side images. It does not establish repeatability or explain the fluctuating 900 rpm images.

Retain incompatible hypotheses: A, the second-120 sample target is achievable after 60 seconds at 900 rpm, while agitation-induced image disturbance causes unnecessary rule-driven continuation; B, genuine gradients remain after 60 seconds at 900 rpm, drive failed optical checks, and useful additional agitation removes them. Neither account is established; bright specks do not identify bubbles.

Proposed six-trial session: two fresh fixed-duration speed pairs, 300 then 900 rpm and 900 then 300 rpm, each stirring exactly 60 seconds without optical restart; then a fresh 900 rpm pair comparing the enabled preferred rule, capped at second 105, with a fixed 60-second stop and shadow-rule logging. Precommit pair order. Use the specified recipe, rinsing, bottle, camera, fixed addition location, references and spill tray; stop if liquid escapes. Record five-second images, depression, specks, commanded speeds, cessation times and stirring duration. Start depth sampling at second 120, alternate depth order within pairs, and report raw readings and every target failure.

residue.text: Decision remains delayed until separating observations arrive. Repeated 300 rpm sample success would support dispensability under these conditions. Timer-stopped 900 rpm success despite failed shadow checks, together with enabled-rule success and longer stirring, would favor A. Timer failure with enabled-rule success would favor B. Both failing, equal durations, or mixed outcomes leave the proposed feedback dependency unresolved.

Prompt image improvement after an externally commanded stop would support an agitation-to-image effect, without identifying bubbles or proving pre-stop uniformity. Enabled and timer trials have different quiet durations before sampling, limiting attribution to added stirring. Sampling disturbance, uncalibrated attenuation, nominal speed, limited replication and order effects remain. Other recipes and processes are untested; no observed total preferred-rule duration establishes existing time savings.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis A: agitation-induced optical disturbance prolongs the rule after a 60-second run can satisfy the bounded final-sample target.
tension.account_b: Hypothesis B: genuine remaining gradients make a 60-second 900 rpm run inadequate, and additional rule-driven agitation achieves the target.
tension.prediction_a: Proposed 900 rpm pair: both final spreads are at most 4 percent, while the enabled rule stirs longer despite timer-trial shadow failures; moving-image spread may fall after stopping.
tension.prediction_b: Same proposed pair: timer-trial final spread exceeds 4 percent and the longer enabled trial meets the target; optical spread tracks residual sample differences. Unequal quiet intervals weaken causal attribution.
